question: Where can I get a list of LNG terminals and underground gas storage facilities in the United States, with location, operator, capacity and status?

answer.summary: Underground storage: EIA's EIA-191 field data (API, monthly to Aug 2026) gives operator, county, Active/Inactive, working gas and max daily withdrawal; PHMSA's annual UNGS file adds exact coordinates. LNG: PHMSA's annual file lists 191 regulated plants (186 in service) with operator, state/ZIP, status and liquefaction/vaporization/tank capacity; EIA's quarterly file gives export trains operating, under construction or approved. Proposed terminals and storage projects are only in FERC PDF maps and Federal Register notices; exact LNG plant positions are restricted (NPMS).
main_caveats: Different publishers measure LNG capacity differently: PHMSA reports maximum liquefaction rate (Sabine Pass 5100 MMCF/D), EIA nameplate per train (6 x 0.59 Bcf/d baseload, 0.76 peak).
PHMSA field TOTAL_CAPACITY_MMCF is maximum vaporization in MMCF per day, not storage volume; LNG tank storage is TOTAL_CAPACITY_BBLS (barrels).
EIA Maximum Daily Delivery is a withdrawal rate. PHMSA injected and withdrawn values are annual volumes. Facility-level maximum injection rates were not verified.
phmsa.dot.gov, ferc.gov and maritime.dot.gov reject automated clients (403); the PHMSA ZIPs are also attached to data.transportation.gov dataset aemm-7pyq, but that copy lags (2024 data).

Offshore LNG deepwater ports are licensed by MARAD, not FERC; FERC lists cover onshore/near-shore terminals only, and most of the 170+ LNG plants (utility peakshavers, satellites) are not FERC-jurisdictional.
answer.confidence_reason: Core EIA and PHMSA files were downloaded and checked; PHMSA 2025 data came from an archived copy, and the FERC PDF maps and MARAD pages could not be read because they block automated clients.

attributes.note: Storage: exact lat/lon per facility (PHMSA) and county (EIA). LNG: state and ZIP (PHMSA) or state only (EIA); no official LNG coordinates published.
attributes.gap_note: LNG plant positions sit in PHMSA's NPMS: PIMMA is restricted to government officials and operators; the public viewer hides LNG plants below ~1:24,000. GEM coordinates are form-gated.

attributes.note: Operator per storage facility and LNG plant (PHMSA operator ID and name; EIA-191 respondent); EIA liquefaction file names the project sponsor.
Storage: working/base/total gas (Mcf or BCF) and max daily withdrawal (Mcf/d); LNG: liquefaction and vaporization MMCF/D, tanks bbl, nameplate Bcf/d-Mtpa. No injection rate.
attributes.gap_note: The sources checked give working volume and withdrawal rates for underground storage. Facility-level maximum injection rates were not verified.

attributes.note: Storage Active/Inactive (EIA); LNG In Service/Retired/Abandoned (PHMSA); export trains operating/commissioning/under construction/approved (EIA); FERC PDF maps add proposed.
attributes.gap_note: No structured official list of proposed LNG import terminals, proposed peakshavers or planned storage projects; they appear only in FERC PDF maps and FERC notices (Federal Register).

sources.name: EIA-191 field-level underground storage data (Natural Gas Annual Respondent Query System, reports RP7 annual and RP8 monthly)
sources.format: JSON (undocumented internal API behind the NGQS web app); Excel export in the web app
sources.summary: Official reservoir-level list of underground gas storage with operator, county, type, Active/Inactive status, working gas, base gas, total capacity and maximum daily delivery.
sources.coverage_note: All U.S. storage operators (mandatory EIA-191); annual 2005-2024 and monthly to August 2026; location only to county.
caveats: Withdrawal rate only; no injection rate.

problems: No published API documentation: endpoint taken from the NGQS web application script (app.min.js).

sources.name: PHMSA Underground Natural Gas Storage (UNGS) Facility annual report data, 2017-present (Form PHMSA F 7100.4-1)
sources.publisher: Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), U.S. Department of Transportation
sources.format: ZIP with CSV (Part A and D, Part B, Part C per year) and XLSX per year, plus a PDF of data fields
sources.license: Public domain (http://www.usa.gov/publicdomain/label/1.0/ per the data.gov record)
sources.summary: Official facility list of underground gas storage with operator, exact coordinates, county, EIA field code and working/base/total capacity in BCF.
sources.coverage_note: 393 facilities, 127 operators, report year 2025; no status field, join to EIA by field code.
caveats: phmsa.dot.gov blocks automated clients; data.transportation.gov copy lags one year.

problems: www.phmsa.dot.gov returns 403 'Access Denied' (Akamai) to automated clients for the data page and the ZIP; tested file is the copy attached to data.transportation.gov (report year 2024, DATAFILE_AS_OF 2/2/2026).
The 2025 report-year figures in this record come from the Wayback Machine copy of the PHMSA ZIP dated 2026-05-08.

sources.coverage_note: 191 plants, 100 operators, report year 2025; status only In Service, Retired or Abandoned.
caveats: No coordinates; no planned or under-construction plants.

sources.name: U.S. Liquefaction Capacity (LNG export projects: existing, under construction and approved)
sources.format: XLSX (sheets Contents, Existing & Under Construction, Approved, Definitions)
sources.summary: Official quarterly list of LNG export terminals by train: status (commercial operation, commissioning, under construction, approved), baseload and peak liquefaction capacity, in-service dates and dockets.
sources.coverage_note: Export only; fully permitted projects only; state-level location; 3Q 2026.
caveats: No import terminals or proposed (unapproved) projects.

if_unstructured.summary: Proposed and planned LNG terminals and storage projects (and their county, capacity and docket) are found in FERC notices published in the Federal Register; the dockets lead to full filings in FERC eLibrary.

local_terms.meaning: PHMSA term for an underground storage facility; Part B of Form 7100.4-1 is filed once per facility.
Storage volume available for withdrawal (EIA in Mcf, PHMSA in BCF); excludes base (cushion) gas.
EIA-191 maximum withdrawal rate in Mcf/day; published as 'Maximum Daily Delivery'.
Utility LNG storage plant for winter peaks; listed by PHMSA, and by FERC only when FERC-jurisdictional.

local_terms.term: Section 3 of the Natural Gas Act
local_terms.meaning: Basis of FERC authority over onshore and near-shore LNG import/export terminals.
FERC stage before a formal application; PF dockets mark planned projects, CP dockets filed applications.
Milestone after which EIA moves an approved export project to under construction.
Offshore LNG terminal licensed by MARAD under the Deepwater Port Act, outside FERC jurisdiction.
